title: Feathered Iced Bakewell Tart with Raspberry Jam
summary: Crisp shortcrust filled with raspberry jam and almond frangipane, topped with white icing feathered with pink raspberry lines.
equipment: small piping bag or paper cone

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
seedless raspberry jam, sieved, for feathering

steps.title: Pastry
steps.text: pulse the flour, icing sugar and salt, pulse in the butter to crumbs, then the yolks and water until it clumps. Flatten into a disc, wrap and chill 1 h. Roll to 3 mm, line the tin, trim and freeze 20 min.

steps.title: Blind bake
steps.text: heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan). Line the case with paper and beans and bake on the tray 20 min, then uncover and bake 5 min more until pale gold. Lower the oven to 175 °C (155 °C fan). Baking the case first keeps the base crisp under the jam.

steps.title: Frangipane
steps.text: beat the butter and sugar 3 min until pale, beat in the eggs one at a time and the almond extract, then fold in the ground almonds.

steps.title: Fill and bake
steps.text: spread the 120 g jam over the base of the warm case, spoon the frangipane on top and spread it gently to the edges. Bake 35-40 min until golden, springy and a skewer comes out clean; the centre should reach 75 °C. Cool completely in the tin.

steps.title: Ice
steps.text: mix the icing sugar and water to a thick but pourable icing and spread it over the cold tart. Pipe thin parallel lines of the sieved jam across it, then draw the cocktail stick through the lines in alternate directions to feather them. Leave 30 min to set. The tart must be cold or the icing will slide off.

tips: A common mistake is overbaking the frangipane, which turns dry; take it out once a skewer comes out clean.
Work quickly when feathering, before the icing starts to set.
Seedless jam gives the neatest layer.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for up to 3 days.
